He is a three-time [[List of NBA All-Stars|NBA All-Star]] and won an [[NBA championship]] with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] and a gold medal with Team USA at the [[2020 Summer Olympics|Summer Olympics]] in 2021. Middleton attended high school at the [[Porter-Gaud School]] in his hometown of [[Charleston, South Carolina]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M Aggies]] from 2009 to 2012. He earned second-team [[List of All-Big 12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big 12]] honors after leading the Aggies in scoring with 14.3 points per game during his sophomore season. Middleton declared for the [[2012 NBA draft]] after his junior season and was selected by the [[Detroit Pistons]] with the 39th overall pick. He saw limited action with the Pistons and spent time with the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] of the [[NBA Development League]] during his rookie season. Middleton was traded to Milwaukee in 2013 and became an immediate contributor to the team. He received his first [[NBA All-Star Game|All-Star]] selection in [[2019 NBA All-Star Game|2019]]. In [[2021 NBA Finals|2021]], Middleton helped lead the Bucks to their first NBA championship since [[1971 NBA Finals|1971]]. The same summer, he won a gold medal at the [[2020 Summer Olympics|Olympics]]. ==Early life and high school career== Middleton was born on August 12, 1991, in [[Charleston, South Carolina]], to James and Nichelle Middleton. He has one older sister named Brittney, and his cousin, [[Josh Powell]], has played in the NBA. Another cousin, [[Kenny Manigault]], played basketball for [[Wichita State University]] and was teammates with Middleton on the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) team Carolina Celtics.{{cite news |last=Bowman |first=Philip |date=August 6, 2008 |title=Pinewood star Manigault commits to Wichita State |url=http://www.postandcourier.com/news/2008/aug/06/pinewood_star_manigault_commits_wichita_49879/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120913195327/http://www.postandcourier.com/news/2008/aug/06/pinewood_star_manigault_commits_wichita_49879/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 13, 2012 |access-date=August 30, 2011 |work=[[The Post and Courier]]}} Two other teammates on the Carolina Celtics accepted Division I basketball scholarships, Jamal Curry ([[Radford Highlanders men's basketball|Radford]]) and [[Devin Booker (basketball, born 1991)|Devin Booker]] ([[Clemson Tigers men's basketball|Clemson]]).{{cite web |title=#22 Khris Middleton |url=http://www.aggieathletics.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=27300&ATCLID=205236051 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120527200850/http://www.aggieathletics.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=27300&ATCLID=205236051 |archive-date=May 27, 2012 |access-date=August 18, 2011 |work=[[Texas A&M Aggies]]}} Middleton attended [[Porter-Gaud School]] and played basketball for the Cyclones under coach John Pearson. As a sophomore, he averaged 12 points and eight rebounds per game.{{cite news |last=Bowman |first=Philip |date=December 6, 2007 |title=Successful spring rockets Khris Middleton up recruiting rankings |url=http://www.postandcourier.com/news/2007/dec/06/overnight_sensation24183/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120906102006/http://www.postandcourier.com/news/2007/dec/06/overnight_sensation24183/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 6, 2012 |access-date=August 28, 2011 |work=[[The Post and Courier]]}} In his junior season, Middleton posted averages of 21 points and 8.6 rebounds per game and was named state player of the year. He repeated as player of the year as a senior, scoring 22.4 points per game and grabbing 8.6 rebounds per game in leading Porter-Gaud to the state title game. Middleton was named Most Valuable Player of the Porter-Gaud Holiday Classic, scoring 22 points in the championship.{{cite news |last=Bowman |first=Philip |date=December 23, 2008 |title=Middleton Powers Cyclones To Victory |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=PZVIAAAAIBAJ&sjid=0AkNAAAAIBAJ&pg=6266,2499232&dq=khris-middleton+porter-gaud&hl=en |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120711195432/http://news.google.com/newspapers?id=PZVIAAAAIBAJ&sjid=0AkNAAAAIBAJ&pg=6266,2499232&dq=khris-middleton+porter-gaud&hl=en |archive-date=July 11, 2012 |access-date=August 31, 2011 |work=[[The Post and Courier]]}} He was nominated for the [[2009 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]], but was not selected to participate.{{cite news |last=Bowman |first=Philip |date=February 19, 2009 |title=Jennings picked for McDonald's All-American game |url=http://www.postandcourier.com/news/2009/feb/19/jennings_picked_mcdonalds_all_american_g72287/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090627035615/http://www.postandcourier.com/news/2009/feb/19/jennings_picked_mcdonalds_all_american_g72287/ |archive-date=June 27, 2009 |access-date=August 31, 2011 |work=[[The Post and Courier]]}} ===Recruiting=== [[ESPN]] ranked him the 64th-best recruit in the Class of 2009, and noted he was the best shooter at his position. Middleton was recruited by [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M]], [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech]], [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]], [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]] and [[Saint Joseph's Hawks men's basketball|Saint Joseph's]]. He chose Texas A&M, and signed with the Aggies on May 30, 2008. He liked the college town atmosphere and got along well with the coaching staff.{{cite news |date=May 30, 2008 |title=Porter-Gaud's Middleton commits to Texas A&M |url=http://www.postandcourier.com/news/2008/may/30/porter_gauds_middleton_commits_texas_a_a42759/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120911105257/http://www.postandcourier.com/news/2008/may/30/porter_gauds_middleton_commits_texas_a_a42759/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 11, 2012 |access-date=August 31, 2011 |work=[[The Post and Courier]]}} {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2005}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Khris Middleton | position = [[Small forward|SF]] | hometown = [[Charleston, SC]] | highschool = [[Porter-Gaud School]] | feet = 6 | inches = 7 | weight = 217 | 40 = | commitdate = May 30, 2008 | scout stars = 3 | rivals stars = 3 | espn grade = 91 }} {{College athlete recruit end | 40 = | year = 2009 | rivals ref title = Texas A&M Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = 2009 Texas A&M Basketball Commits | espn ref title = | rivals school = tamu | scout s = 186 | espn schoolid = | scout overall = 30 (SF) | rivals overall = 29 (SF) | access-date = August 28, 2011 | bball = yes }} ==College career== ===Freshman year=== Middleton was recruited by then-Texas A&M assistant coach [[Scott Spinelli]]. Coming into his freshman year, Middleton expected to fill the [[three-point shooting]] void of departed senior [[Josh Carter]]. Middleton's college career started slowly, connecting on 1-of-12 [[field goal (basketball)|field goals]] in limited action of his first three games.{{cite news |last=Zwerneman |first=Brent |date=February 13, 2010 |title=Freshman Middleton in middle of action for A&M men |url=http://www.chron.com/sports/college/article/Freshman-Middleton-in-middle-of-action-for-A-M-men-1708248.php |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121022010458/http://www.chron.com/sports/college/article/Freshman-Middleton-in-middle-of-action-for-A-M-men-1708248.php |archive-date=October 22, 2012 |access-date=August 31, 2011 |work=[[Houston Chronicle]]}} After a season-ending leg injury to Derrick Roland on December 11, 2009, Middleton was forced to take a larger role in the offense and started 18 of the last 20 games. On February 3, 2010, he scored 16 points to help Texas A&M erase an 11-point second-half deficit to defeat [[2009–10 Missouri Tigers men's basketball team|Missouri]] 77–74.{{cite news|first=Steve|last=Walentik|url=http://www.columbiatribune.com/news/2011/jan/15/well-worth-the-wait/|title=A&M's Middleton no longer a surprise|work=[[Columbia Daily Tribune]]|date=January 15, 2011|access-date=September 1, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120404022810/http://www.columbiatribune.com/news/2011/jan/15/well-worth-the-wait/|archive-date=April 4, 2012}} In a 69–53 [[2010 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] round of 64 victory over [[2009–10 Utah State Aggies men's basketball team|Utah State]], Middleton scored a season-high 19 points on 7-of-10 shooting.{{cite news |date=March 19, 2010 |title=Middleton helps Texas A&M snag fifth straight opening round win |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=300780245 |url-status=unfit |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121107132900/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300780245 |archive-date=November 7, 2012 |access-date=October 6, 2024 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]]}} Texas A&M's season ended with a loss in the round of 32 to [[2009–10 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|Purdue]]; the Aggies finished with a record of 24–10.{{cite news |date=March 21, 2010 |title=Kramer takes over to lead Purdue to sixth Sweet 16 in 12 appearances |url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300802509 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120107140544/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300802509 |archive-date=January 7, 2012 |access-date=September 2, 2011 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]]}} Overall, Khris Middleton averaged 7.2 points and 3.7 rebounds per game and led the team in scoring five times. ===Sophomore year=== As a sophomore, Middleton led the team and finished ninth in the Big 12 in scoring at 14.3 points per game while also contributing 5.2 rebounds per game. He hit 45 percent of his shots from the floor and 78.4 percent of his [[free throw]]s. Middleton scored in excess of 10 points in 27 games and led the team in scoring 16 times. He scored a career-high 31 points in a 71–62 overtime victory over [[2010–11 Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball team|Arkansas]], including 11 of the team's last 12 points in regulation. Middleton was impressed with Kennedy's coaching acumen and chose to remain an Aggie.{{cite news |last=Burch |first=Jimmy |date=July 7, 2011 |title=New Texas A&M's new basketball coach will install faster pace |url=http://www.star-telegram.com/2011/07/07/3207616/new-texas-ams-new-basketball-coach.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120902153926/http://www.star-telegram.com/2011/07/07/3207616/new-texas-ams-new-basketball-coach.html |archive-date=September 2, 2012 |access-date=August 28, 2011 |work=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]]}} He was listed on the preseason watchlist for the [[Wooden Award]].{{cite web |last=Katz |first=Andy |authorlink=Andy Katz |date=October 3, 2011 |title=Scouting the Wooden Award watch list |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/7053604 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111031142136/http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/7053604/opposing-coaches-break-50-players-wooden-award-watch-list-college-basketball |archive-date=October 31, 2011 |access-date=October 29, 2011 |work=[[ESPN]]}} Middleton was a unanimous choice to the preseason All-Big 12 team.{{cite web|url=http://www.big12sports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=106110&SPID=13134&DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=10410&ATCLID=205312119|title=Preseason All-Big 12 Men's Basketball Honors Announced|work=[[Big 12 Conference]]|date=October 6, 2011|access-date=October 29, 2011|archive-date=November 6, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211106212706/https://big12sports.com/news/2011/10/6/205312119.aspx|url-status=live}} Despite being the preseason co-favorite in the league, Texas A&M finished 14–18 overall and 4–14 in the [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]]. The team was hampered by a rash of injuries, including a knee injury that forced Middleton to sit for 12 games. He averaged 13.2 points and five rebounds per game, down from the previous season. On April 9, 2012, Middleton declared for the NBA draft, forgoing his final season of collegiate eligibility. He thanked Texas A&M in a statement.{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2012/story/_/id/7794122/2012-nba-draft-khris-middleton-texas-aggies-declares|title=Khris Middleton declares for draft|access-date=July 9, 2015|date=April 10, 2012|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|archive-date=July 10, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150710191719/http://espn.go.com/nba/draft2012/story/_/id/7794122/2012-nba-draft-khris-middleton-texas-aggies-declares|url-status=live}} ==Professional career== ===Detroit Pistons (2012–2013)=== ====2012–13 season: Rookie season==== Middleton was selected by the [[Detroit Pistons]] with the 39th overall pick in the [[2012 NBA draft]]. On December 6, 2013, he scored a then-career-high 29 points in a 109–105 win over the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20131206/MILWAS/gameinfo.html|title=Notebook: Bucks 109, Wizards 105|date=December 6, 2013|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=December 16, 2014|archive-date=December 24, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141224021317/http://www.nba.com/games/20131206/MILWAS/gameinfo.html|url-status=live}} ====2014–15 season: First playoff appearance==== On December 15, 2014, the Bucks were down by one to the [[Phoenix Suns]] with under four seconds remaining in regulation as Middleton hit a contested game-winning buzzer beater to defeat the Suns, 96–94, with Middleton finishing with 14 points.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141215/MILPHX/gameinfo.html|title=Middleton's late shot helps Bucks beat Suns 96–94|date=December 15, 2014|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=December 16, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141228003205/http://www.nba.com/games/20141215/MILPHX/gameinfo.html|archive-date=December 28, 2014|url-status=dead}} On March 7, 2015, he scored a then-career-high 30 points on 11-of-20 shooting in a 91–85 win over the Washington Wizards.{{cite web|url=https://www.brewhoop.com/2015/3/7/8169043/bucks-vs-wizards-final-score-khris-middleton-career-high-john-wall|title=Recap: Middleton scores career-high in win vs Wiz|first=Dan|last=Sinclair|date=March 7, 2015|website=Brew Hoop|access-date=September 6, 2021|archive-date=September 6, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210906142413/https://www.brewhoop.com/2015/3/7/8169043/bucks-vs-wizards-final-score-khris-middleton-career-high-john-wall|url-status=live}} In his second season with the Bucks, Middleton emerged as an important "3-and-D" player, shooting 46.7 percent from the floor and 40.7 percent from behind the three-point arc. He averaged 13.4 points, 4.4 rebounds and 2.3 assists per game.{{cite news|last=Herbert|first=James|title=Report: Bucks, Khris Middleton agree to 5-year, $70 million deal|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nba/eye-on-basketball/25230079/report-bucks-khris-middleton-nearing-5-year-70-million-deal|access-date=July 9, 2015|work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=July 1, 2015|archive-date=July 10, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150710145314/http://www.cbssports.com/nba/eye-on-basketball/25230079/report-bucks-khris-middleton-nearing-5-year-70-million-deal|url-status=live}} ====2015–16 season: New contract==== On July 9, 2015, Middleton re-signed with the Bucks to a five-year, $70 million contract, with a player option for the fifth year.
